stories.title: Wall Street opens August bracing for Friday's jobs report as the biggest week of earnings season begins
key_points: US stock futures rose Monday, with Dow futures up **265 points (0.9%)** as August trading opened.
Friday brings the **July jobs report** — economists expect just **87,500 new jobs**, with unemployment ticking up to **4.3%**.
**Palantir** reports today, with **AMD, Eli Lilly and SanDisk** also headlining this week's earnings.
Of the roughly **300 S&P 500 companies** that have already reported, **85% beat expectations**.
Today's **ISM manufacturing index** — a survey of factory activity — is the first data point of the week.
stories.background: Each month, the US government's jobs report (officially the 'Employment Situation Summary') tells investors and the Federal Reserve how healthy the labor market really is — a weak number can mean the economy is slowing, while a too-strong one can worry the Fed about inflation. Coming into August, the second-quarter earnings season has been unusually strong, with the vast majority of large US companies beating Wall Street's profit forecasts. That combination — solid earnings, but a labor market that's expected to keep cooling — is what traders are weighing as the month opens.
stories.what_happened: US equity futures climbed Monday morning as investors kicked off August trading, with contracts tied to the **Dow Jones Industrial Average** up 265 points (0.9%), **S&P 500** futures up 0.55%, and **Nasdaq-100** futures up 0.93%. The day's first economic release is the **July ISM manufacturing index**, a widely watched gauge of US factory activity. **Palantir Technologies** reports earnings after the close today, kicking off a week that also includes **AMD, Eli Lilly and SanDisk**. The week's centerpiece is Friday's **July nonfarm payrolls report**, where economists polled by Dow Jones expect the economy added **87,500 jobs**, up from June's 57,000, while the unemployment rate is forecast to edge up to **4.3%** from 4.2%. So far this earnings season, roughly 300 S&P 500 companies have reported, and **85% have beaten analyst expectations**, according to FactSet.
stories.why_it_matters: The jobs report is one of the single most-watched pieces of economic data because it directly shapes what the Federal Reserve does with interest rates — a weak print can raise hopes for rate cuts (which tend to lift stocks), while a hot one can do the opposite. A cooling labor market alongside strong corporate profits is an unusual mix that makes this week's data pivotal for where markets go next.
stories.ripple_effects: A weaker-than-expected jobs number Friday would likely fuel bets on Fed rate cuts, which tends to weaken the US dollar and lift growth and tech stocks; a stronger number could do the reverse. Earnings from Palantir, AMD and Eli Lilly will move AI, semiconductor and pharma stocks specifically, and since US markets set the tone globally, Asian and European indices — plus INDIA's Sensex and Nifty, which have their own catalysts this week — often take cues from how Wall Street reacts.
stories.why_now: August trading always opens with this rhythm — a fresh jobs report and a fresh batch of earnings — but this week matters more because the jobs data is expected to show renewed labor-market cooling just as the earnings season is proving unusually resilient.
stories.watch_next: Friday's July nonfarm payrolls report and unemployment rate, plus Palantir's earnings reaction after markets close today.

key_terms.definition: The US government's monthly count of jobs added outside of farming — the single most-watched snapshot of how the labor market is doing.
A monthly survey of purchasing managers at US factories; a reading above 50 signals factory activity is expanding, below 50 signals contraction.

stories.the_lesson: Markets react less to whether news is 'good' or 'bad' in isolation and more to whether it matches or beats what was already expected — a jobs report that's merely 'okay' can still move markets sharply if it surprises against consensus forecasts.
stories.market_link: US equity futures (Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq-100), plus Palantir, AMD, Eli Lilly and SanDisk shares directly on their earnings; Friday's jobs number will move rate-cut expectations and the dollar.

stories.title: A Kuki-Zo civil body gives Manipur's government 48 hours before threatening a total shutdown
key_points: The **WCKCSOs-Ukhrul**, a Kuki civil society body, has given the state government **48 hours** to end an alleged blockade on supplies to Kuki-Zo areas.
It has threatened a **total shutdown from August 5** if the issue isn't directly addressed.
The group accuses authorities of allowing the **confiscation and burning** of essential commodities headed to Kuki-Zo villages.
It follows a **counter economic blockade on National Highway-202** the same group imposed from July 26.
A separate blockade by Naga and Meitei groups on **National Highway-2** has continued for nearly a month with little government intervention.
stories.background: Manipur has been gripped by **ethnic conflict between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities since May 2023**, which killed hundreds and displaced tens of thousands, splitting the state into informally segregated zones. Kuki-Zo areas in the hills depend heavily on national highways passing through Meitei-dominated valley areas for essential supplies like food, fuel and medicine, making these highways frequent flashpoints and leverage points for both communities. Civil society organisations on both sides — rather than only political parties — have increasingly driven blockades and counter-blockades as a form of protest and pressure on the government.
stories.what_happened: The **Working Committee of Kuki Civil Society Organisations (WCKCSOs)-Ukhrul** issued a **48-hour ultimatum** to the Manipur government, demanding it end what the group calls a selective blockade that has allowed essential commodities bound for Kuki-Zo inhabited areas to be **confiscated and burned**. The group warned of a **total shutdown starting August 5** if the government does not directly address the issue. This follows the same body's own **counter economic blockade on National Highway-202**, in force since midnight of July 26, which it says will continue until the government guarantees free movement of essential goods — though it has carved out exemptions for medical emergencies, passenger travel, airport-bound travelers and security forces. Separately, a blockade on **National Highway-2** by Naga and Meitei groups near Senapati and Kanglatongbi has continued for nearly a month without effective government intervention.
stories.why_it_matters: Overlapping blockades on Manipur's two main highway lifelines threaten to cut off essential supplies to hundreds of thousands of people across ethnic lines, more than two years after the conflict first erupted. It's a fresh test of whether the state and central governments can de-escalate tensions that have repeatedly flared even during periods of relative calm.
stories.ripple_effects: A total shutdown would hit fuel, food and medical supply chains into Kuki-Zo hill districts, worsening humanitarian conditions already strained by the broader conflict. Continued highway blockades also disrupt trade and travel through Manipur, a key corridor to India's northeast, and can draw in central paramilitary forces if tensions escalate.
stories.why_now: The ultimatum follows weeks of tit-for-tat blockades since late July, with the Kuki body's frustration mounting after it says government assurances on protecting supply movement went unmet.
stories.watch_next: Whether the Manipur government responds before the 48-hour deadline lapses, and whether the threatened August 5 shutdown actually goes into effect.

key_terms.definition: A deliberate disruption of the movement of goods and supplies, used here as a form of political protest by community groups rather than a government or military action.

stories.the_lesson: In regions with unresolved ethnic conflict, control over a handful of physical supply routes can become as powerful a bargaining chip as any political demand.

stories.title: Bharti Airtel reports Q1 results today, with analysts penciling in a ~45% profit jump
key_points: Airtel's board meets today, **August 4**, to sign off on results for the quarter ended June 30.
Analysts expect net profit to rise **26–45% year-on-year**, with some estimates near **₹8,639 crore**.
Revenue is expected to grow around **15%**, helped by steady subscriber additions and 5G rollout.
**ARPU** (average revenue per user) is forecast to tick up to roughly **₹261/month**, a key profitability gauge.
It's one of **114 companies** reporting results today as India's Q1 earnings season hits its peak, alongside ONGC, Marico and DLF.
stories.background: Bharti Airtel is India's **second-largest telecom operator** by subscribers, competing chiefly with Reliance Jio and Vodafone Idea in a market that consolidated from more than a dozen players a decade ago to effectively three. Airtel has spent heavily to roll out **5G networks** across India and has steadily raised prepaid and postpaid tariffs in recent years to improve profitability after a brutal price war in the 2010s nearly wiped out smaller rivals. ARPU — how much revenue the company earns per subscriber each month — is the industry's single most-watched number because it shows whether tariff hikes are sticking without driving customers away.
stories.what_happened: Bharti Airtel is set to announce its **April–June (Q1 FY27) results** on August 4, with its earnings call scheduled for the following day. Ahead of the announcement, analysts polled by financial outlets expect **net profit to jump 26–45% year-on-year**, with some estimates as high as **₹8,638.60 crore**, alongside roughly **15% revenue growth**. Brokerages are watching subscriber additions (expected around 50–60 lakh net adds for the quarter), a modest uptick in ARPU to about **₹261**, and progress in turning Airtel's heavy 5G investment into sustained profit. The results land on one of the busiest days of India's Q1 earnings season, with **114 companies** — including ONGC, Pidilite, Marico, DLF, Sun Pharma Advanced Research, Aditya Birla Capital, Bosch and Shree Cement — also due to report.
stories.why_it_matters: Airtel is a bellwether for both the health of India's telecom sector and consumer spending more broadly, since phone bills are one of the most universal household expenses. A strong ARPU number would confirm that Indian consumers are absorbing recent tariff hikes without switching providers or cutting usage, which matters for how much pricing power telecoms retain going forward.
stories.ripple_effects: A profit beat or miss moves not just Airtel's stock but sentiment across the telecom sector, including rivals Reliance Jio (part of Reliance Industries) and Vodafone Idea. Because so many companies report today, the results collectively will help set the tone for Indian equity markets this week, just as the **RBI's rate decision** (due Wednesday) also looms.
stories.why_now: Q1 FY27 (April–June 2026) is Airtel's first full quarter to reflect the latest round of tariff increases and expanded 5G coverage, making today's numbers an important read on whether that strategy is working.
stories.watch_next: The actual reported numbers later today, and management's commentary on the earnings call August 5 about further tariff hikes or 5G monetization plans.

key_terms.definition: Average Revenue Per User — how much money a telecom company earns, on average, from each subscriber per month; a key measure of pricing power.

stories.the_lesson: In industries with just a few large players (like Indian telecom), a single company's ARPU trend often reveals more about the whole sector's pricing power than any one earnings report suggests.
stories.market_link: Bharti Airtel (NSE: BHARTIARTL) results will move the Nifty Telecom index and could ripple into how investors price Reliance Jio and Vodafone Idea.

stories.title: India's stock exchanges quietly switch to an auction-based closing price for F&O stocks
key_points: From **August 3**, SEBI's new **Closing Auction Session (CAS)** sets closing prices for F&O-eligible stocks.
It replaces the old **VWAP-based** method with a **single-price auction**, matching all buy/sell orders at once.
Continuous trading for these stocks now ends at **3:15pm**, followed by the auction window until **3:35pm**.
Non-F&O stocks are **unaffected** — they keep trading normally until 3:30pm.
The goal: **harder-to-manipulate closing prices** and better execution for large institutional orders.
stories.background: Every trading day, exchanges need an official **'closing price'** for each stock — it's used to value mutual funds, settle derivative contracts, and calculate index levels. Until now, India used a **Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP)** method for stocks with **F&O (futures & options)** contracts — essentially an average of prices over the last few minutes of trading. Critics have long argued VWAP-based closes can be nudged by large last-minute trades, especially on days when derivative contracts expire, because a trader with a big options position has an incentive to move the underlying stock's closing price in their favor.
stories.what_happened: **SEBI (India's markets regulator)** and the **NSE** launched the **Closing Auction Session (CAS)** on **August 3, 2026** for all F&O-eligible stocks. Under the new system, continuous trading for these stocks stops at **3:15pm**, then a **Closing Auction Session** runs until **3:35pm**, where all outstanding buy and sell orders are pooled together and matched at a single **'equilibrium price'** — the price at which the maximum number of shares can be traded. That single matched price becomes the official closing price. Non-F&O stocks continue trading normally until 3:30pm with no change, while F&O derivatives themselves trade until 3:40pm with a brief post-close session from 3:50-4:00pm.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a **market-plumbing change**, not a headline event, but it affects how fairly prices are set for some of India's most-traded stocks — including everything used to value index funds and settle options contracts that ordinary investors' mutual funds and pensions are exposed to.
stories.ripple_effects: Expect brokers and trading algorithms to adjust their end-of-day strategies around the new 3:15-3:35pm window; index-fund managers who need to trade 'at the close' will now route orders into the auction instead of the last few minutes of continuous trading. Over time, regulators expect this to reduce the kind of expiry-day price manipulation SEBI has flagged in past investigations.
stories.why_now: The change took effect this week (from August 3), making it a fresh, live shift in how Indian markets actually operate right now.
stories.watch_next: Whether closing-price volatility for F&O stocks measurably drops in the weeks after the switch, and how index funds adapt their trading around the new auction window.

key_terms.definition: Derivative contracts that let traders bet on or hedge against a stock's future price — India restricts these to its most liquid, heavily-traded stocks.
Volume Weighted Average Price — an average stock price weighted by how many shares traded at each price, historically used to set India's closing prices.

stories.the_lesson: How a price is calculated — not just what the price is — shapes whose interests get protected; regulators often redesign these unglamorous 'plumbing' rules specifically to close loopholes that sophisticated traders were quietly exploiting.
stories.market_link: Affects daily closing prices and settlement for all NSE/BSE F&O-eligible stocks and any index fund or derivative tracking them.

stories.title: Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj wins its first big Bihar seat as bypoll results split three ways

thread.previously: We reported that vote counting was underway in three state assembly bypolls — Bankipur (Bihar), Datia (Madhya Pradesh), and Manjalpur (Gujarat) — with Prashant Kishor's new Jan Suraaj Party chasing its first big electoral win in Bankipur, a seat BJP had held.
thread.changed: The results are in: Jan Suraaj's Prashant Kishor won Bankipur decisively, defeating the BJP candidate by more than 19,000 votes — a landmark first major win for his two-year-old party. The other two seats split along expected lines: Congress won Datia in Madhya Pradesh, and BJP retained Manjalpur in Gujarat.

key_points: **Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj Party** won its first big electoral test, taking Bankipur in Patna.
Kishor beat BJP's Neeraj Kumar Sinha by more than **19,000 votes** (63,203 to 44,250).
RJD finished a distant **third** with around 14,000 votes — a blow to the opposition's Bihar strategy too.
**Congress won Datia** (Madhya Pradesh) and **BJP retained Manjalpur** (Gujarat) — no upsets there.
The seat opened up after BJP's state president **Nitin Nabin** vacated it to join the Rajya Sabha.
stories.background: **Jan Suraaj** ('Good Governance') is the political party launched by election strategist **Prashant Kishor** — the man who has advised winning campaigns for Congress, BJP, and several regional parties over the years — after he decided to build his own party in Bihar rather than keep working behind the scenes for others. Bankipur, a BJP stronghold in Patna represented by the party's own state president until he moved to the Rajya Sabha (parliament's upper house), was seen as a tough test: a symbolic win here for Jan Suraaj would signal it can actually convert Kishor's strategist fame into real votes, not just headlines.
stories.what_happened: Vote counting concluded on **August 3** for bypolls in three states. In Bihar's **Bankipur** constituency, Jan Suraaj's Prashant Kishor defeated BJP's Neeraj Kumar Sinha by more than **19,000 votes**, polling **63,203 votes** to Sinha's **44,250**, with RJD's Rekha Kumari trailing in third with about 14,000. In **Madhya Pradesh's Datia** seat, Congress won, and in **Gujarat's Manjalpur** seat, BJP retained control as expected. The Bankipur seat had fallen vacant after sitting BJP MLA and state party president Nitin Nabin was elected to the Rajya Sabha in April.
stories.why_it_matters: This is Jan Suraaj's **first genuine electoral proof point** since Kishor founded the party — a single bypoll win doesn't rewrite Bihar's political map, but it gives Kishor real momentum and a talking point heading into future state elections, where he's positioned Jan Suraaj as a alternative to both the BJP-led NDA and the RJD-Congress opposition bloc.
stories.ripple_effects: Expect Jan Suraaj to use this win to recruit more local leaders and candidates ahead of bigger Bihar contests, while BJP and RJD both face pressure to explain losing ground in a seat/state they've historically fought over between themselves. It also validates Kishor's strategy of contesting as a standalone third force rather than allying with an existing bloc.
stories.why_now: The results were officially declared today, resolving the count that was underway as of yesterday's report.
stories.watch_next: Whether Jan Suraaj can turn this single-seat win into a real organizational push — more candidates, more local wins — before Bihar's next major electoral test.

key_terms.definition: A mini-election held for a single seat that becomes vacant between general elections — often seen as an early signal of voter mood.

stories.the_lesson: A single bypoll win is a real signal, not proof of a lasting shift — new parties need to win repeatedly, in different places, before a one-off victory becomes an actual political trend.
